Commentary.Commentary: On the whole, 196 should not be too difficult for Bangladesh. But if Windies bowl well and take a few quick wickets, it will be interesting to see the response. Join us back at 5.15 pm local (1115 GMT).

Superb bowling from Bangladesh. They concentrated on just bowling consistent lines and lengths and did not over-attack. They were not at their best on the field, dropping 4 catches, yet, it never seemed like they got frustrated. Mehidy and Shakib, who opened the attack, were economical while Mustafizur and Mortaza picked up 6/65 amongst themselves in 20 overs combined. Rubel also would have had a great outing but he lost the plot at the death. His first 8 overs went for 32 but his final 2 yielded 29.

Poor batting effort from the Windies, yes, but one cannot fault them totally. They tried everything. First, they looked to settle in and then play their shots. Could not get much runs. Then, they tried Hetmyer's approach - slogging wildly and get quick runs, did not muster anything. It was during the Chase-Paul stand that the batters actually got used to the pitch but by then it was too late.

The openers took their time, biding out the spinners with Shai Hope keeping the innings steady. However, the collapse started at the fall of Bravo's wicket. The second wicket fell at 64 and the Windies then slipped down to 127/6, before a breezy 51-run stand between Roston Chase and Keemo Paul took them close to 200.

The Windies will be disappointed to say the least - 195 is not what one expects after electing to bat. But the fact that they were 127/6 with not many batsmen left to come will make them feel a bit better. Overall, they were consumed by the two-paced deck.

Then trudges off. Big, big hole now for the Windies.

Bangladesh surprised everyone by opening the bowling with two spinners and even though they managed to pick just a solitary wicket, the runs have been curtailed. Windies though, will back themselves to do some power-hitting in the later overs but they need to plan it out. In the next 20-odd overs, they at least need to get 4 runs an over and then get 100 in the last 10. Wickets in hand are a must.

Okay then. The players are out in the middle. Shai Hope and Kieran Powell are the openers for the Windies. Spin first up. Mehidy Hasan to bowl with the first new ball. Powell to face. Here we go!

Bangladesh captain, Mashrafe Mortaza, says that Bangladesh have been going alright this year, especially in this format. Wants to finish this year well now. Adds that this is a very important game, the first one and wants to set the tone straight. On picking three seamers in the playing XI, Mashrafe says that in England, three seamers would be required, so the hosts are planning from now itself. On losing the toss, Mortaza says that chasing has been the forte. Then cheekily says that he is not sure what are the Windies doing and smiles when he is informed about the same.

Windies captain, Rovman Powell, says that the decision is based on the fact that the pitch looks a good one to bat on. On his captaincy debut, Rovman smiles and says that it is a great experience and wants to win this series. On spin being their weakness, Powell says that in the last few days, they have practiced a lot against spinners in the nets and hopes that it comes good in this game. On some players coming back into the side - like Carlos Brathwaite and Darren Bravo, Rovman is excited to see that experience in the playing XI.
TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin. Mashrafe Mortaza spins the coin, Rovman Powell calls Heads and it is a Head. WINDIES CHOOSE TO BAT.
PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo doing the pitch report observes that it looks like a good batting surface. There is a bit of grass but it is well rolled over.

Bangladesh batting coach Neil McKenzie is pleased with the way the home side has developed so far. Admires the way the lower order is also contributing with the bat. Informs that in the last 5 matches, Bangladesh have had 7 different centurions in the white-ball matches, which is a good competition for spaces. Is very happy to welcome Tamim Iqbal back in the side but is happier that even in his absence, the others stepped up. On Zimbabwe's bowling comparison with the Windies', McKenzie says that the Rhodesians tested Bangladesh while the Windies stretched India in India, with the likes of Thomas and the spinners doing well, so does not want to take them lightly.
WEATHER - It is bright and sunny in Mirpur, with no forecast of rain.

Hello and welcome to the first ODI between Bangladesh and Windies in Mirpur. The hosts will go as the favourites in this encounter because they have their bases covered. Tamim Iqbal's return will boost them more. On the other hand, Windies would like to improve themselves in the ODI series. Carlos Brathwaite and Darren Bravo's return will boost them but they will again be without their regular captain Jason Holder. Rovman Powell will be leading the side. This is the favourite format of Shimron Hetmyer who will look to be all guns blazing. What's in store for us? Stay tuned.
